title: Dispatch: provider-neutral context-packet renderer (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch 1 of 3 for W10 (`eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, ADR 0020 transition design section
7 and 12.3). Parent authority: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, and
`docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md`
sections 7.1, 7.2, 7.3.

WORKTREE `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.12.1`, BRANCH `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.1`, cut
from `eshyra-o9bd.19.12`. Dependencies are installed. Touch nothing outside it.

## What this dispatch delivers, and nothing more

The provider-neutral RENDERER that turns a built context packet into the text a
DM would actually receive, plus its unit tests. It is a pure function over an
already-built packet. It does NOT inject anything, does NOT touch the
orchestrator, does NOT touch `shadow.ts`, `measurements.ts`, `packet.ts`,
`retention.ts`, or any test under `packages/core/test/discovery/` other than a
new file of your own. Injection is dispatch 3's job; M12 is dispatch 2's.

## Code survey (verified at 71c322f, read these before writing)

- `packages/core/src/discovery/types.ts` — `ContextPacket`, `PacketCandidate`,
  `ProjectionLimitNote`, `CapabilityPreflight`, `DiscoveryRoute`,
  `TypedTraversal`, `RetentionOverflow`, `DiscoveryTrace`.
- `packages/core/src/discovery/packet.ts:285-432` — how `packetCandidate()`
  fills each field. Note especially: for a rules record `sourceProse` is
  `{ data: <the whole record.data object> }`; for an adventure entity it is the
  entity object itself. `identity.kind` is the record kind or the literal
  `'adventure-entity'`.
- `packages/core/src/discovery/packet.ts:117-164` — the three
  `ProjectionLimitNote` kinds (`success-branch`, `area`,
  `execution-readiness`), each carrying `note`, `evidence` and
  `preservedProse`.
- `packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRules.ts:101-121` —
  `CampaignRuleProjection` / `CampaignRulingProjection` fields. These are
  `eshyra-jhpt`-owned. Read them; never redefine them, never declare a local
  rule or ruling shape (design section 8.4; the analyzer in
  `packages/core/test/discovery/support/discoveryOwnership.ts` enforces it and
  WILL fail you).
- `packages/core/src/rules/types.ts` — `RulesAmbiguity` (`id`, `question`,
  `interpretations[]`, `canonicalResolution`, always `null` in the pack).
- `packages/core/src/orchestrator/contextAssembler.ts:982` —
  `renderContextMessage`, for house style: `## Section` headings joined by
  blank lines, `- ` bullets, no JSON dumps of prose.
- `packages/core/src/discovery/traceDerivation.ts:260-405` — the derived trace
  shape carrying `retention.overflow` and `packet.byteOverflow`. Your input
  type must be satisfied by BOTH the live `DiscoveryTrace` and this derived
  trace.

## The deliverable

New file `packages/core/src/discovery/packetMessage.ts`, exporting:

```ts
export interface RenderablePacketTrace {
  readonly retention: { readonly overflow: readonly RetentionOverflow[] };
  readonly packet: {
    readonly packet: ContextPacket;
    readonly byteOverflow: readonly RetentionOverflow[];
    readonly dropped: readonly {
      readonly candidateKey: string;
      readonly band: CandidateBand;
      readonly routes: readonly DiscoveryRoute[];
      readonly reason: string;
    }[];
  };
}

export interface RenderedContextPacket {
  readonly text: string;
  readonly bytes: number;           // Buffer.byteLength(text, 'utf8')
  readonly candidateCount: number;
  /** Every must-consider candidate a budget could not hold, from BOTH budgets. */
  readonly mustConsiderOverflow: readonly RetentionOverflow[];
  /** Design section 12.3: presence is never evidence of use. Always null. */
  readonly modelUsageClaim: null;
}

export function renderContextPacketMessage(
  trace: RenderablePacketTrace,
): RenderedContextPacket;
```

Add both types and the function to `packages/core/src/internal.ts` beside the
existing `buildContextPacket` export. Do NOT add them to the root
`packages/core/src/index.ts` (AGENTS.md: new core symbols default to internal).

## What the rendered text must contain, and why

Design section 7.1 lists the required per-candidate content. Every one of these
must appear in the TEXT, not merely be reachable in the object — the text is
what a DM receives.

Per retained candidate, in packet order:

1. **Identity** — `key`, `kind`, `name`.
2. **Provenance** — `sourceRef`, `locator` when present, `source` label, and
   the licence identity. A rules-record candidate whose `provenance.sourceRef`
   is empty must be rendered with an explicit `unattributed` marker rather than
   an empty field; design section 7.3 forbids presenting a record as
   authoritative merely because it was retrieved, and M8's standing structural
   check is exactly "reached the packet carrying no source attribution".
3. **Source prose, VERBATIM.** Walk `sourceProse` and emit every string-valued
   leaf as RAW TEXT under its JSON pointer path. Do not `JSON.stringify` a
   string leaf: an escaped `\"` or `\n` is no longer the source text, and the
   fixture corpus's field-9 `exactSubstring` facts are matched against what the
   DM can read. Non-string leaves (the typed projections) are rendered
   separately under a heading that states plainly that they do not replace the
   prose above.
4. **Every retrieval route** — route class AND the trigger detail for each.
5. **Traversed relationships** — source record, link field, relation, target,
   one line each.
6. **Known source ambiguity** — `id`, `question`, every interpretation id, and
   the canonical resolution stated as absent when `canonicalResolution` is
   null. Never present an interpretation as the answer.
7. **Applicable campaign rules and rulings** — for each, the identity, kind,
   scope, provenance, effective position, and supersession status
   (`supersededBy` / `revokedPosition` rendered explicitly, including when they
   are null), plus the governing record keys and the prose when present, and
   for a ruling its ambiguity id and selected interpretation id. The governing
   source material stays present and attributed beside them — that is satisfied
   by rendering rules inside their candidate's block, never in a detached list.
8. **Deterministic capability.** When `capability` is present, render it as a
   POSITIVE BOUNDED CONTRACT: the operation, the capability id, the revision,
   the status, the required inputs, the explicit exclusions, and the residual
   DM interpretation. When `capability` is absent, render exactly the negative
   form the parent bead requires: no capability was positively selected, AND an
   explicit statement that this is not a claim that the record has no
   mechanics, that it is irrelevant, or that it is safe to ignore. Never infer
   a capability from the presence of typed fields.
9. **Projection limits, in band.** Each `ProjectionLimitNote` must be rendered
   INSIDE its own candidate's block, adjacent to the typed projection it
   qualifies — not collected into a trailing appendix. A partial projection
   whose limits are disclosed three hundred lines away is not disclosed in
   band, and design section 7.2's two worked cases
   (`creature:adult-black-dragon` `/data/actions/5` success branch and area;
   `spell:fireball` missing typed area) are the cases this must hold for.

Packet-level, once:

10. **Must-consider overflow.** Concatenate `retention.overflow` and
    `packet.byteOverflow`. If non-empty, the text must carry an explicit
    overflow section naming EVERY dropped must-consider candidate, each of its
    routes, and the reason recorded by the producer. A must-consider candidate
    never disappears silently.
11. **Other drops.** Every `packet.dropped` entry whose band is not
    `must-consider` is rendered with its candidate key and the producer's
    recorded reason. Reasons are the producer's strings; never author a
    replacement reason here.

Explicitly NOT in the text:

- No coverage figure, completeness figure, readiness score, or candidate
  percentage. No "N of M rules found". Design section 13.2.
- No statement that the material was, will be, or should be used, and no
  instruction that presence implies relevance. `modelUsageClaim` stays `null`
  on the value and no equivalent claim appears in the prose.
- No re-ordering, summarizing, truncating, or paraphrasing of source prose. If
  a record's prose is long, it is long.

## Structural rules for the implementation

- The renderer is TOTAL and pure: no I/O, no `Date`, no randomness, no reads of
  the db or the pack. Same input, byte-identical output.
- An empty packet (`candidates: []`) with no drops and no overflow renders a
  block that says the run retained nothing, not an empty string. Design section
  13.3 forbids a green-looking nothing; a caller must be able to tell "the
  renderer produced nothing" from "discovery retained nothing".
- `bytes` is the UTF-8 byte length of `text`. It is NOT `ContextPacket.bytes`
  (which counts the serialized JSON) and must not be copied from it.
- Derive `mustConsiderOverflow` from the two producer lists. Do not recompute a
  band, do not re-derive an exclusion from "absent from `candidates`". W9's
  canonical-events doctrine applies: a reason you did not receive is a reason
  you may not invent.

## Evidence required (new file
`packages/core/test/discovery/packetMessage.test.ts`)

Build real packets through the existing offline path — `runDiscoveryStages`
from `packages/core/src/discovery/harness.ts` with the probe scenarios in
`packages/core/test/discovery/support/scenario.ts`, exactly as
`packages/core/test/discovery/discoveryProbes.test.ts` does. Do not hand-author
a `ContextPacket` literal for the worked cases; a renderer proven only against
invented input proves nothing about the real pack.

E1. **Verbatim prose.** For `spell:fireball` and `creature:adult-black-dragon`,
    assert the exact source substrings appear in `text` unescaped — including
    at minimum "a 20-foot-radius sphere" and the Acid Breath "or half as much
    damage on a successful one". Assert the text contains no `\\n` or `\\"`
    escape sequence originating from a prose field.
E2. **In-band limits.** For both worked cases, assert the projection-limit note
    appears between that candidate's heading and the NEXT candidate's heading —
    an index comparison, not a bare `toContain`. Assert `spell:fireball`'s area
    note and `creature:adult-black-dragon`'s success-branch note are each
    present with the producer's own `note` string.
E3. **Projection is not readiness.** Assert the typed-projection heading states
    that the projection does not replace the source prose, and that a candidate
    with projection limits and no capability renders NO capability contract.
E4. **Capability positive form.** With P8's capability declaration
    (`magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3`, operation `hit-target` — see
    `packages/core/test/diagnostics/probes/p08Ammunition.ts` and how
    `discoveryProbes.test.ts` supplies `declaredCapabilities`), assert the
    rendered contract names the operation, the revision, every declared input,
    every declared exclusion, and the residual interpretation.
E5. **Capability absence.** For a candidate with no capability, assert the
    text carries the "no capability positively selected" form AND the explicit
    disclaimer that this is not "no mechanics", not "irrelevant", and not "safe
    to ignore".
E6. **Campaign rule and ruling presentation.** Using the jhpt seam fixtures in
    `packages/core/test/discovery/support/jhptCampaignRules.ts`, assert a
    placed house rule and a placed ruling each render identity, kind, scope,
    provenance, effective position, supersession status, and — for the ruling —
    ambiguity id and selected interpretation id, all inside the governing
    candidate's own block.
E7. **Must-consider overflow.** Drive a real overflow by running the stages
    with a `budget` small enough to overflow (both `maxCandidates` and, in a
    second case, `maxPacketBytes`). Assert both overflow sources reach
    `mustConsiderOverflow` and that every overflowed candidate key, each of its
    route classes, and the producer's reason string appear in `text`.
E8. **Ambiguity.** Assert an ambiguity renders its question and every
    interpretation id, and states the canonical resolution is absent.
E9. **Non-claims.** Assert `modelUsageClaim` is `null`, and assert the text
    matches no coverage/score/percentage pattern and contains no claim of use.
E10. **Empty and deterministic.** Assert the empty-packet block is non-empty
    and distinguishable, and assert two renders of the same trace are
    byte-identical.

## Non-negotiables

- `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing.
- Biome is canonical; CI fails on warnings. Do not suppress a finding.
- Do not weaken, skip, or reshape any existing test.
- Do not edit `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, anything under `.claude/`, or the
  design document. If the design looks wrong, record it in your notes with
  `bd update eshyra-o9bd.19.12.1 --append-notes` and file a follow-up with
  `bd create`; do not fix it here.
